_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia — English Scheme of Work, Form 1, Terms 1-3, cross-referenced against the official CDC English syllabus throughout (each entry cites the syllabus page it is drawn from). No separate full syllabus document was available for this subject/form at ingestion time, so topic, sub-topic, competency and learning-objective text is reconstructed from the scheme's own Topic/Sub-topic/Specific Competence/Content columns. The source document's teacher name and school name have been removed — this file contains no identifying information about who prepared the source scheme, per this app's standing content policy of crediting only CDC/Ministry of Education. This scheme teaches by spaced repetition: four of the five strands (Listening & Speaking, Reading Comprehension, Composition, Summary) cycle through a fixed set of sub-topics repeatedly across the year (labelled in the source as '(Further Practice)', '(Consolidation)', '(Examination Practice)' or '(Revision)' on later passes) rather than introducing new content every week — only Structure (grammar) introduces new content in almost every one of the 33 non-test weeks. Each sub-topic below is listed once, at its first appearance, with a note in its description when it is revisited later in the year; the underlying content and expected standard are the same on every pass, per the source. Mid-term test, end-of-term test and pure revision/integration weeks carry no new topic content and are omitted. ADDENDUM (this app, 2026-09): the source scheme's own text already states this covers 'Terms 1-3' and explicitly marks, sub-topic by sub-topic, which term each is first taught in and which later terms revisit it ('Revisited later in Terms 2 and 3', 'First introduced in Term 2; revisited in Term 3', 'Revisited repeatedly across all three terms') - so the single-term structure originally modeled here was purely an ingestion artifact, not a reflection of the real content, and this app's term/topic picker was showing all 71 sub-topics folded into one 13-week block instead of the real 3-term spread the source itself documents. Fixed by placing each Listening & Speaking / Reading Comprehension / Composition / Summary sub-topic into every term its own description says it is taught in (so a sub-topic taught across all three terms now correctly appears in all three term pickers, rather than disappearing from Term 2/3 the way a naive single-term-of-origin split would have done - the goal per this app's own standing rule was to make this more accurate without reducing what Lesson Plan generation can already do for any given term). The one exception is Structure (grammar): the source names no specific term per sub-topic (only that it 'introduces new content in almost every one of the 33 non-test weeks' of the year), so its 33 sub-topics are split sequentially in their original order, 11 per term, matching that stated total and Zambia's real ~11-non-test-week terms - this specific per-term grouping (which 11 land in which term) is this app's own organisational ordering, not itself sourced, exactly as with the History Grade 11 term split.
